pr_title: Fix panics when m-mapping head chunks
pr_body:
NOTE: This is pointing to the release branch.

Fixes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/10291
Fixes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/10315

~I will test it out in our dev environment today or on Monday. So please don't merge/release a new version until then. It will have to wait a few days :(~ Done

cc @beorn7 as you are the release shepherd
pr_comments: I think this should fix the bug, great work! I added a few comments, mainly about locking

It would take me a long time to do a serious review of the code itself, but I fully trust @replay here.

Once this has been verified to work in our test environment and once @replay 's comments are addressed, this should totally go into a patch release

@replay thanks for the reviews, I will fix them today.

Since Beorn is on vacation today, I will take the responsibility of doing the patch release.

Another point of information: we tested this in our dev environment and can verify that this fixes the panic (we were able to reliably reproduce the panic by setting scrape interval to 1m and then restarting the Prometheus after a few hours and waiting).

issue_context.title: Panic after failed m-map file replay due to corruption
issue_context.body:
As described in https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/10291#issuecomment-1044373110, if there was a m-map file corruption and we ended up deleting a bunch of m-map files during replay, we are not updating the expected next file in the async queue recently introduced in https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/10051. This can cause similar panic as #10291.

I am working on a fix along with #10291.
comments: Closed by https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/10316, will be fixed in v2.33.4

review_comments: is there a chance that len(pendingDeletes) == 0 ?
If there was any error, that means there was at least 1 file that was not deleted. So no, it will be >0 if there was an error.

Isn't it possible that `DeleteCorrupted` will delete all files in the fs? In that case this would have to be set to `0`.

I'm starting to wonder if it wouldn't be easier to just add a method to `ChunkDiskMapper` which looks at the fs to determine the highest present chunk and then returns its sequence, similar like what happens in `openMMapFiles()`. This could then be used here and also in `openMMapFiles()`, not in `Truncate()` though because at the point where `Truncate()` is called there might chunks in the queue.

What do you think about this?

`lastSeq` starts at 0, and will be never set if all files are deleted. So it will be 0, right?

And about checking fs to determine the last sequence: I thought about that, but error handling becomes more complect. What if traversing the directory gives and error? What do we do then?

> lastSeq starts at 0, and will be never set if all files are deleted. So it will be 0, right?

you're right, thanks for clarifying. I just noticed one more thing though... `cdm.mmappedChunkFiles` is a map, which means we'll iterate over its keys in random order. So before assigning `seg` to `lastSeq` we should check if `seq > lastSeq`, no?
